items.title: Development and Innovative Applications of Tools for Monitoring Neuronal Electrical Activity
items.summary: Neuronal electrical activity provides the most direct dynamic readout of excitability, synaptic transmission, circuit coordination, and information processing in the nervous system. Monitoring tools have evolved from intracellular and patch-clamp recordings that resolve ion-channel and membrane currents to high-density extracellular arrays, flexible neural interfaces, optical activity indicators, wireless implants, and artificial intelligence-assisted decoding systems. items.title: Are cortical microcircuits optimized for information flux?—A simulation-based reverse engineering study
items.summary: Introduction A sufficiently large information flux in recurrent neural networks, quantified by the mutual information between successive network states, has been proposed as a marker of rich information-processing capabilities. This raises the question of whether biological neural networks, such as cortical microcircuits, may be structurally organized to enhance information flux. Methods To investigate this possibility, we study a simplified model of the cortical layer 5 architecture, in which a densely and strongly interconnected core population is embedded within a larger supporting network.

items.title: Familial risk for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and related behaviors in toddlerhood are preliminarily associated with altered frontoparietal development in infancy measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy
items.summary: Introduction Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood neurodevelopmental disorder associated with impairments across the lifespan. Children with ADHD have been found to have delayed brain maturation. These delays may be present and detectable with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) as early as infancy for children at familial risk for ADHD. The present study examined longitudinal changes in functional connectivity among infants at high and low familial risk for ADHD, and their association with ADHD-related behaviors in toddlerhood. items.summary: The following paper presents the design of a spiking neural network (SNN) based neuromorphic signal processing system that can be used in low power embedded smart sensors to perform real time detection of audio events. items.title: Global context integration for pharmacologically robust preclinical sleep stage classification
items.summary: Sleep stage classification from electrophysiological signals is essential for studying brain function in preclinical neuroscience, yet models often fail to generalize across subjects and experimental conditions, particularly under pharmacological interventions that alter neural and muscular activity. We propose a robustness-oriented deep learning framework that integrates multi-branch feature extraction, global contextual representation, sequence modeling, and training strategies designed to reduce sensitivity to subject- and treatment-specific variability. items.summary: This independent undergraduate research paper examines the relationships between environmental stress, seasonal nutrition, physical activity, and human endurance performance. Using the Southern Appalachian Mountains of North Carolina and the highlands of Papua New Guinea as comparative environments, the study investigates how elevation, temperature, humidity, snowfall, rainfall, and seasonal sunlight may influence physiological adaptation and psychological well-being. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. items.title: Jointly predicting courses and grades using a transformer-based model
items.summary: Existing predictive models in learning analytics often treat student academic history as a simple sequence, overlooking the concurrent nature of courses taken within a semester. This simplification can lead to inaccurate performance predictions, particularly for students with heavy or challenging course loads.
